prompt.context: Our client is an advertising firm with $400 million in annual profits based in the United States with operations all around the world. The client primarily generates revenue through digital display format advertisements and is evaluating whether it should invest resources in alternative digital format ads that are emerging.
prompt.question: What should our client do?

clarifying_info.a: Static image and/or text based ads found on web pages. One of the largest sources of online advertising revenue.

clarifying_info.q: What does the client do exactly?
clarifying_info.a: The client is a leading digital advertising demand and supply-side firm — it connects advertising brands on the demand-side (like P&G and Coca Cola) to online publishers on the supply-side (like ESPN and NYTimes.com).

clarifying_info.q: Are the market data figures global or U.S. only?
Is there overlap between mobile and video advertising?
clarifying_info.a: Video is an ad creative format and mobile is a platform. Video ads can run on either mobile or desktop platforms, so mobile advertising includes video advertising.

clarifying_info.q: Who are the market leaders in global video advertising?
clarifying_info.a: Google and AOL will be the leaders with expected shares of 40% and 25% respectively, and those shares will remain constant throughout the forecast horizon.

clarifying_info.q: How much of the remaining video market can the client compete for?
clarifying_info.a: There are two other competitors in the peer group and the client's RMS is 1 with both. There is 10% of the market that the client cannot compete in due to existing contractual agreements. It will take the client one year to build the commercial relationships needed to operate in this market.

exhibits.title: Online Advertising Market
exhibits.shows: A table showing the global online advertising market size (USD billions) from 2012 to 2019 across four segments: Display advertising, Search advertising, Mobile advertising, and Video advertising.

exhibits.title: Projected Resources Needed by Department
exhibits.shows: A table showing projected annual costs by department for the client to enter the video advertising market, with Year 1 costs and ongoing costs listed separately.

framework: Market sizing: size the alternative digital ad format markets (mobile, video, search) and forecast growth trajectories
Competitive position: assess the client's ability to win share in target markets given existing capabilities and relationships
Investment required: estimate fixed and variable costs (engineering, sales, marketing) to enter the new market
Revenue and profitability: calculate expected revenue given achievable market share and compare to investment cost
Strategic recommendation: recommend whether and how to enter, including sequencing and next steps

questions.prompt: Looking at Exhibit 1, what observations do you make about the digital advertising market and what it means for the client?
questions.guidance: A strong answer notes: (1) Display advertising has been the largest segment but growth is flattening (~$10bn to $22bn over 8 years, slowing). (2) Mobile and video are growing rapidly — both will match or exceed display by 2019. (3) Video is the fastest-growing segment (1bn to 30bn, 30x in 8 years). (4) Since video is a format and mobile is a platform, mobile advertising growth is partly driven by video. The implication is that display is the client's core but a maturing market; video/mobile represent the most attractive growth opportunities.

questions.prompt: Given the market data and cost structure in Exhibit 2, calculate the client's expected revenue, costs, and profit from entering the video advertising market for 2016-2019.
questions.guidance: Walk through the market share derivation first, then build the table. Key insight: costs are trivial relative to revenue, so this is a highly attractive opportunity.

math.setup: Step 1 — Derive client market share in video advertising. Google = 40%, AOL = 25%, leaving 35%. Of that, 10% is off-limits due to contractual agreements, leaving 25% addressable. The client and two competitors share the 25% equally (RMS = 1 with both), so client share = 25% / 3 ≈ 8.3% ≈ 8%. Step 2 — Apply 8% share to video market size each year. Step 3 — Annual costs = Engineering + Sales + Marketing (year 1: $50K + $300K + $20K = $370K; ongoing: midpoint ~$25K + ~$350K + $30K = ~$405K). Note: client can only enter after year 1 of relationship-building, so first revenue year is 2016 (using 2016 market size of $15bn).
steps: Market share derivation: 100% - 40% (Google) - 25% (AOL) = 35% remaining; 35% - 10% (contractual exclusions) = 25% addressable; 25% / 3 competitors = ~8% per competitor
math.answer: Client revenue grows from $1.2bn in 2016 to $2.4bn by 2019. Costs are negligible ($350K-$460K/year). The opportunity could more than triple the client's current $400M profit in year 1 alone.

recommendation: The client should enter the video advertising market. The video segment is the fastest-growing in digital advertising (30x growth 2012-2019) and the client can achieve approximately 8% market share, generating $1.2bn+ in revenue in year 1 — far exceeding its current $400M annual profit.

The cost to enter is minimal (under $500K/year) given that much of the technological infrastructure already exists; the primary investment is in building a new sales force and commercial relationships.
risks: Market share assumption depends on RMS remaining at 1 with two competitors — new entrants or consolidation could erode share
The 1-year ramp-up period to build commercial relationships creates a window where competitors could strengthen their positions
Google and AOL's 65% combined share leaves limited addressable market; further consolidation could squeeze the available pool
Revenue estimates assume flat competitive dynamics and no pricing pressure as video supply increases
next_steps: Identify target verticals (e.g., CPG, automotive, entertainment) and the specific brands and media buying agencies within those verticals to acquire as clients
Hire and onboard the video advertising sales team immediately to begin the relationship-building process
Evaluate whether to build video ad technology in-house or acquire/partner with an existing video ad tech vendor to accelerate time to market
Define KPIs for the first 12 months (relationships signed, revenue pipeline, share capture) to track entry progress
